additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410999-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] SuspendedEV CRM:00921001608
additional_info.body:
Dear Szymon,
I hope you're doing well. Thank you for your patience as we've taken some time to analyze the issue.
The session was stopped on 2025-02-20 at 14:34:14 from the EV side, as the SOC of the vehicle reached 100%.
Timestamp
: 2025-02-20T14:34:14.036324+00:00
Log Message:
swcpu [user:debug] [4022] [DCC] | 2025-02-20T13:28:18 | DC1: | EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=0 | EVSE_MaxCur[A]=0 | EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=0 | EVSE_NowCur[A]=0 | EVSE_NowVol[V]=1.3 | EV_TarCur[A]=0 | EV_TarVol[V]=0 | EV_SOC[%]=100 | EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=150 | Pilot=2
As the session terminated from the EV side, the status message showed "SuspendedEV". As the plug was not removed, so DC1 remained in the "B1" state, which is normal behavior for us.
At 2025-02-20, 14:50:55, the StatusNotification command was sent from the OCPP backend. As a result, DC1 briefly displayed "SuspendedEV" for a second.
Log Entries:
2025-02-20T14:50:55.689327+00:00

Send command: StatusNotification
(b6755b12-6b8d-4fc4-a558-5e7294ccf6ad) - {"connectorId":0,"errorCode":"NoError","status":"Available"}
2025-02-20T14:50:55.778707+00:00
sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/4dd497458d8c[734]: OCPP: Received result: StatusNotification (b6755b12-6b8d-4fc4-a558-5e7294ccf6ad) - {}
2025-02-20T14:50:56.686564+00:00
sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/4dd497458d8c[734]: OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (b536e7f5-1052-4c9e-bedb-0cf30e93b12c) - {"connectorId":1,"errorCode":"NoError","status":"SuspendedEV"}
2025-02-20T14:50:56.688593+00:00
sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/4dd497458d8c[734]: OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (39adbccf-519d-4a4a-b657-cd4edafef746) - {"connectorId":2,"errorCode":"NoError","status":"Available"}
Afterward, when the connector was unplugged at 2025-02-20, 14:52:03, the pilot state transitioned from "B1" to "A", and just 2 seconds later, the DC1 status notification changed from "SuspendedEV" to "Available."
Regarding your second query about why the status was not changed to "Preparing":
The status of DC1 did not change because the connector was not unplugged from the EV. Therefore, the pilot state remained in "B1" until the connector was unplugged at 2025-02-20, 14:52:03. After just 2 seconds, the status was updated to "Available." There were no issues from the charger or the backend, and the billing was processed correctly.
Regarding the unsuccessful charging sessions for DC1:
We have analyzed several charging sessions and observed that some sessions were not authorized, while others failed due to an invalid idTag. DC1 had successful charging sessions starting from 2025-02-22.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410999-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] SuspendedEV CRM:00921001608
additional_info.body:
Hello,
yes please elaborate on the topic because:
- the station behaved exactly as you wrote: charging finished, the station indicated SupsendedEV, then the plug was unplugged and the pilot status went to “A” status and CP was available - but only for the station because the SuspendedEV status remained in the backend system.
The status remained because the station did not send a Finishing message about the completed charging session.
I spoke with MSP (the backend provider) and he explained to me that the station should send a Finishing message after the session is completed and the session is terminated based on that.
Here is the whole problem, that SuspendedEV remained, the point in the backend was further occupied. Therefore, the next session was rejected, because for the backend this point was occupied. This was the result of this, not properly terminated session.
Why didn't the charger send Finishing?
Best regards,
Szymon

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410999-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] SuspendedEV CRM:00921001608
additional_info.body:
I am curious about this point of the OCPP 1.6 protocol:
Does the charging station behave in the manner indicated here? That is, it has a setting of false for StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect and that is why the charging station sent SuspendedEV after this session ended.
I don't know if this is a good indication, but it is a suggestion.
The whole problem here is the session termination on the backend system side.
As we can see, this system did not terminate the session even though it received an Available status - because its logic requires Finishing.
Where does the problem lie:
- In SICHARGE D, which did not send Finishing?
- In the backend system that did not terminate the session seeing Available?
- Is it enough to change the StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect parameter to true and then the sessions will be terminated as expected? How to check if the station supports this message?
The OCPP information is from a publicly available file from the OCA website: OCPP-1.6 edition 2.
Please feel free to analyze.
With best regards,
Szymon Brodowicz
Siemens Sp. z o.o.
Smart Infrastructure

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410999-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / P9 170000982] SuspendedEV CRM:00921001608
additional_info.body:
Hello,
I attached word with cases which we have, the main issue is that we have suspended EV message after stop transaction. Backend provider said that it is critical mistake.
For now, we ask them to use:
OCPP configuration key "TxStopPoint"
PowerPathClosed -> StopTransaction message when CCS plug is removed
EnergyTransfer -> StopTransaction message when EcoG reports a Session End
With best regards,
